source_text: En cui luci, cui populo sententiarum, cui dignitati iudiciorum tradux tua et convitium facere non timet et conatur inferre praeiudicium. Hic dubium non est, quia non te pudeat illud dicere, quod videtur reliquum, id est ut respondeas veram Prophetae, immo Dei per Prophetam esse sententiam, insuperabilem prudentum rationem, qua docetur iniquissimum, ut peccata parentum filiis imputentur.
pass_a_gloss: Behold to what light, to what people of sentences, to what dignity of judgments your vine-layer both does not fear to make insult and tries to bring a prejudgment. Here it is not doubtful, because you are not ashamed to say that which seems remaining, that is that you answer that the sentence of the Prophet, nay of God through the Prophet, is true, the unconquerable reason of the prudent, by which it is taught most unjust that parents' sins be imputed to sons.

lemmas.lexica: LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: Look at the light, the crowd of pronouncements, the dignity of judgments that your inherited sin is unafraid to insult and tries to overrule! Here there is no doubt you will not be ashamed to say what seems the only remaining reply: the prophet’s pronouncement—or rather God’s through the prophet—is true, and the reasoning of wise people is invincible, teaching that charging children with their parents’ sins is utterly unjust.

choices.why: For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: Explicitly discusses the prophet’s pronouncement on personal righteousness and guilt rather than inherited guilt.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
